report.source_text: Physical examination: The general condition was good, and there were no abnormalities in the system inspection. Specialized examination: Bilateral breasts are symmetrical, with average breast development. Bilateral nipples were normal and there was no nipple discharge. A red and swollen area of 3 cm × 2 cm in size could be seen in the left armpit, accompanied by ulceration and a small amount of secretions (Fig. 1A). A mass of approximately 3.0 cm × 2.0 cm in size could be palpated in the left armpit, which was hard and had a clear boundary, with moderate activity. No obvious abnormal mass could be palpated in the right breast, and no obvious enlarged lymph nodes could be palpated in the right armpit.

report.source_text: Laboratory and auxiliary examinations: Blood routine, coagulation, and bowel and bowel routine tests were all normal. No abnormalities were found in liver and kidney function, electrolytes, blood sugar, and blood lipids. The myocardial enzyme spectrum and tumor 7 items were all within the normal range. Hepatitis A, B, C, human immunodeficiency virus, and syphilis showed no significant abnormalities. Among the 5 items of thyroid function, anti thyroglobulin antibodies were 188.50 IU/mL, and anti thyroid microsomal antibodies were > 1000.0 IU/mL. The electrocardiogram indicated sinus rhythm and changes in some lead T waves. Chest and abdominal computed tomography plain scan showed several miliary lesions in both lungs and hepatic steatosis. No obvious abnormalities were found in the gallbladder, pancreas, spleen, kidneys, and bladder. No obvious abnormalities were found on plain and enhanced dual breast magnetic resonance imaging scans. Breast ultrasound indicates hypoechoic areas in both breasts, considering the possibility of breast adenosis, the United States of America breast imaging reporting and data system Class 2, bilateral lipoma, and left axillary lymph node enlargement.

report.source_text: The postoperative pathology of the left axillary mass combined with morphological and immunohistochemical results was consistent with Paget disease. The pathological examination of the skin lesions showed an abundance of keratinization in the epidermis, a large number of atypical cells in the epithelial layer, infiltration of interstitial lymphocytes, and infiltration of Paget cells in the superficial dermis (Fig. 2). Postoperative immunohistochemistry showed estrogen receptor (+, 20%), progesterone receptor (−), human epidermal growth factor receptor-2 (3+), Ki-67 (30%), cytokine (CK)7 (+), and p63 (−) (Fig. 3).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 57-year-old woman presented with a left axillary mass present for over 2 years, which had increased in size recently with skin ulceration. Physical examination confirmed a 3.0 x 2.0 cm red, swollen, ulcerated, hard mass with clear boundaries in the left axilla and no nipple abnormalities or discharge. Imaging studies including breast MRI and ultrasound showed no suspicious breast lesions. Laboratory tests including tumor markers were normal except for elevated thyroid autoantibodies. The crucial diagnosis was confirmed postoperatively by pathological examination of the left axillary mass, which showed epidermal keratinization, numerous atypical epithelial cells, lymphocyte infiltration, and Paget cells in the superficial dermis. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated ER positivity (20%), PR negativity, HER2 overexpression (3+), Ki-67 proliferative index of 30%, CK7 positivity, and p63 negativity, consistent with Paget disease.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Clinical examination revealed a 3.0 x 2.0 cm red, swollen, ulcerated, hard mass in the left axilla with clear boundaries and no nipple abnormalities or discharge
Imaging and laboratory tests showed no breast malignancy and normal tumor markers, but elevated thyroid autoantibodies
Postoperative pathology showed keratinization, atypical epithelial cells, lymphocyte infiltration, and Paget cells in superficial dermis of left axillary mass
Immunohistochemistry of the mass showed ER (20%) positivity, PR negativity, HER2 (3+) overexpression, Ki-67 (30%), CK7 positivity, and p63 negativity, confirming Paget disease

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Negative breast MRI and ultrasound with no nipple involvement or discharge; pathology consistent with Paget cells in axillary skin
